description: Composite figure of five images: panel (a) consists of four in-situ HEXRD diffraction patterns and panel (b) is a line plot with an inset curve. Each (a) sub-panel plots Intensity (×10^4 counts) on the y-axis (0.00-0.20, ticks 0.05) against 2θ (degree) on the x-axis (ticks 10.0, 10.5, 11.0, 11.5) for two overlaid curves — red = RD and blue = TD, with an orange diamond legend entry marked FCC — at a different true strain printed top-right: ε=0.14, ε=0.22, ε=0.3 and ε=0.38. Peaks are annotated α211 (near 10.0°), γ311 (near 10.8°), γ222 (near 11.3°) and α220 (near 11.6°); green circles mark the α (BCC) reflections and orange diamonds the γ (FCC) reflections. The γ311/γ222 intensities fall markedly with increasing strain while α211 stays high, and in the ε=0.3 and ε=0.38 panels a black arrow labelled BCT points to asymmetry on the low-angle shoulder of α211. Panel (b) plots Martensite Fraction (%) (0-25) versus True Strain (0.0-0.5) as red solid circles (RD) and blue open circles (TD); both start near zero and RD lies clearly above TD beyond ~0.15 strain, reaching the highest values at the largest strain. The inset plots Strain Hardening Rate (MPa, 1250-2500) versus True Strain, the RD curve rising to a local maximum near 0.3 strain while TD stays lower and then drops steeply. The panels together argue that the RD steel undergoes faster strain-induced α'-martensite formation, which explains its higher strain-hardening ability.

observations.observation: Each diffraction sub-panel of (a) plots Intensity (×10^4 counts) on the y-axis (0.00-0.20, tick spacing 0.05) against 2θ (degree) on the x-axis (ticks at 10.0, 10.5, 11.0 and 11.5).
The four diffraction sub-panels are labelled with true strain values ε=0.14, ε=0.22, ε=0.3 and ε=0.38 in their top-right corners.

Peaks in (a) are annotated α211 (near 10.0°), γ311 (near 10.8°), γ222 (near 11.3°) and α220 (near 11.6°), with green circles marking the α BCC reflections and orange diamonds marking the γ FCC reflections.
The legend given in the ε=0.3 panel defines the red curve as RD, the blue curve as TD and the orange diamond symbol as FCC.

At ε=0.14 and ε=0.22 the red (RD) and blue (TD) α211 peaks are of similar height, whereas from ε=0.3 onward the red RD α211 peak is clearly higher than the blue TD peak, i.e. RD shows more BCC/martensite signal at high strain.
In the ε=0.3 and ε=0.38 panels a black arrow labelled BCT points to an asymmetry (shoulder) on the low-angle side of the α211 peak.
The γ311 and γ222 (FCC) peak heights decrease noticeably from ε=0.14 to ε=0.38 while the α211 peak height remains approximately unchanged, indicating loss of austenite.
Panel (b) plots Martensite Fraction (%) (y-axis 0-25, ticks every 5) against True Strain (x-axis 0.0-0.5, ticks every 0.1) with red circles for RD and blue open circles for TD.
In (b) both curves start close to zero at low strain and the RD curve lies visibly above the TD curve from roughly 0.15 true strain onward, with the separation growing with strain.

The inset of (b) plots Strain Hardening Rate (MPa) (y-axis 1250-2500) versus True Strain (0.0-0.5); the RD curve shows a local maximum at intermediate strain while the TD curve stays lower and flatter before a steep final drop.

The caption states that (a) shows the variation of different diffraction peaks with true strain of the two samples and that (b) shows the martensite fraction calculated by the Rietveld refinement method as a function of true strain, with the inset showing the corresponding strain hardening rate curves of the two samples.

The citing text states that at the elastic stage (true strain below ~0.03) the martensite fraction is negligible, less than 1 vol.%, so the transformation in this steel occurs mainly during plastic deformation.
The citing text states that the difference in martensite fraction between the two samples can be as high as 4 vol.% at a true strain of ~0.48, the uniform elongation of the TD sample.

The citing text states that a black arrow in (a) marks BCC peak asymmetry appearing above ~0.3 true strain, that peak separation was considered error-prone at lower strains, and therefore the increase in martensite fraction was set equal to the reduction in austenite fraction.
The citing text states that the RD sample shows higher martensite transformation kinetics than the TD sample, which explains its higher strain hardening ability particularly above ~0.2 true strain.

subfigures.description: HEXRD pattern (intensity ×10^4 counts vs 2θ/degree, ~9.8-11.8°) at true strain 0.14 with red RD and blue TD curves almost coincident. Peaks annotated α211, γ311, γ222, α220; green circles mark α (BCC) and orange diamonds γ (FCC) reflections. Largest peak is α211 near 10.0°.
Same axes at true strain 0.22. The red (RD) curve already slightly exceeds the blue (TD) curve at the α211 and α220 positions; γ311 and γ222 are lower than at ε=0.14.

Diffraction pattern at true strain 0.3; the red RD curve is distinctly higher than blue TD at α211 and α220. A black arrow labelled BCT marks a low-angle shoulder on the α211 peak. This panel carries the legend: red line RD, blue line TD, orange diamond FCC.

Diffraction pattern at true strain 0.38; γ311/γ222 peaks are considerably reduced relative to α211/α220, the RD-TD gap at α211 is widest, and the BCT arrow again marks asymmetry of the α211 peak. The x-axis label is partially cropped at this panel's lower edge.

Martensite Fraction (%) versus True Strain (0.0-0.5) with red filled/open circles for RD and blue open circles for TD. Both curves rise from near zero; RD is consistently above TD from ~0.15 strain and reaches the highest plotted values near true strain 0.5.

Strain Hardening Rate (MPa, y from 1250 to 2500) versus True Strain (0.0-0.5) for RD (red) and TD (blue). Both drop steeply from an initial high value, pass through a minimum near 0.1-0.15 strain; RD then rises to a local maximum around 0.25-0.3 strain before decreasing, whereas TD remains at a lower, flatter level and falls steeply near the end.

unreadable_items: The legend (red RD / blue TD / orange diamond FCC) is only printed in the ε=0.3 sub-panel, not in the ε=0.14 and ε=0.22 sub-panels
The x-axis label of the fourth diffraction sub-panel (ε=0.38) is partially cropped at the lower edge
No numeric values are printed on the curves of (b) or on the inset; the end-point fractions can only be read against the gridlines
Strain-hardening-rate values in the inset cannot be read exactly because the curves lie on a coarse grid with no data labels
